facts.text: A non-specialist author should keep a dissent log with columns for claim, expert positions, evidence cited, consequence if unresolved, proposed test and accountable decision owner.
facts.quote: Keep a dissent log with columns for claim, expert positions, evidence cited, consequence if unresolved, proposed test and accountable decision owner.

facts.text: A non-specialist author should maintain three separate categories throughout the document—verified fact, expert judgment and management assumption—and never mix them.
facts.quote: Maintain three categories throughout the document and never mix them: verified fact, expert judgment, management assumption.

facts.text: The recommended preparation sequence calls for 8 to 12 Critical Decision Method interviews in months 1 to 2, covering safety, simulation, test, assessor and operations.
facts.quote: Months 1 to 2: 8 to 12 Critical Decision Method interviews (safety, simulation, test, assessor, operations).

facts.text: The recommended preparation sequence calls for IDEA-style elicitation of durations and probabilities in month 2.
facts.quote: Month 2: IDEA-style elicitation of durations and probabilities.

facts.text: The recommended preparation sequence calls for a pre-mortem with skeptics present in month 3.
facts.quote: Month 3: pre-mortem with the skeptics present.

facts.text: The recommended preparation sequence calls for an independent red team in month 4.
The recommended preparation sequence calls for a gate review with recorded dissent in months 5 to 6.
facts.quote: Months 5 to 6: gate review with recorded dissent.
